title: Migrations on a device you cannot log into

videos.script:
A server's database is migrated once, by somebody watching. {{server}} A phone's is migrated a million times, by the app, at seven in the morning, with nobody there to read the error.

So the migration has to be boring. {{steps}} A number in the file, and a list of steps, each one moving it one version on. You write the planner's four.

Then you test them from every version that ever shipped. {{paths}} A phone left in a drawer for a year arrives at version four from version one. The update that only knows the last step fails on it.

Then a migration fails halfway, twice. {{broken}} Statement by statement, it leaves a database no version of the app can open. In a transaction, it leaves the old one, whole.

And last, the button that makes the error go away by deleting the database. {{destroy}} On a phone that works offline, it deletes the only copy.
